cells.tense: You are here, with your hand on the mix, and it is working.
cells.ask: Name what you have finished and pass it to one person who did not help make it.
cells.core:
You can feel when to add and when to take away, and you do it without stopping the thing to think about it. What is in front of you holds more than one thing at once — tight and loose, loud and quiet, yours and theirs — and you are not torn by it. You are in the middle of it, and the middle is not a compromise.

This is integration you can stand in. The gauges are live, the hands are moving, and the result is a thing someone else can receive. What that gives you to do next is small and outward: name what is finished and pass it along to someone outside the work. The balance holds because you let it leave. Keeping it longer only makes it heavier.
cells.sheetLine: You hold the whole thing at once and keep it moving.
cells.verb: adjusting the blend until it flows
cells.place: where what has gathered is finished and let go

cells.tense: You are bracing for a room that has not formed yet and tuning to it early.
cells.ask: Say the disagreement once, plainly, to the person it belongs to, and leave the room before you smooth it over.
cells.core:
You are smoothing things before they have had a chance to be rough. A disagreement starts and you are already blending it, finding the version where no one is wrong, and the whole thing goes down easy. That ease is costing you something. The distinctions that were trying to form get folded back in before anyone sees them.

The flow is being protected at the expense of the flow. What you are avoiding is not conflict — it is difference that would let the work get sharper. You do not need to reach for a fight. Just let one distinction stand long enough to be heard. The finishing you are good at gets better when the pieces have actually met.
cells.sheetLine: You smooth the rough parts before they can teach you anything.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that closed behind you, and the room has scattered.
cells.ask: Tell one person the small thing you noticed today, without explaining why it matters.
cells.core:
Nothing holds its shape long enough to be finished. Something arrives, you engage, and before it can gather you are already turned toward the next thing. The center is not there to come back to because you have not stopped anywhere long enough to have one. This is not laziness. It is a gathering that has run low.

What restores it is not more effort in the middle. It is contact — one other person, actually met, where you are seen and they are seen, no merging. That kind of exchange puts current back into the place that integrates. So start smaller than the whole. Say one true thing to one person and let it land. Finishing gets easier when something has been received.
cells.sheetLine: Nothing gets finished because nothing gets held long enough.

cells.tense: The pen is already moving in a room you keep saying you are only passing through.
cells.ask: Point to one thing you shaped this week and say out loud that you shaped it.
cells.core:
You are integrating all the time — sorting, blending, deciding what belongs — and you describe it as just how things went. The work of holding complexity happens, and the credit goes to the situation. You are in the middle of it, adjusting, and you present yourself as a participant rather than the one doing the adjusting.

The shaping is real and it is running. What is missing is the saying so, and you can hear it in how you tell the story. Something simpler is available: the transmission you already do, teaching or passing on what you have gathered, is the same line at its root. Name the shaping, and the flow gets a sender.
